name.en: JEE Main Registration (Joint Entrance Examination Main)

description.en: JEE Main (Joint Entrance Examination Main) is a national-level entrance examination conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) for admission to undergraduate engineering and architecture programmes at NITs (National Institutes of Technology), IIITs (Indian Institutes of Information Technology), CFTIs (Centrally Funded Technical Institutions), and other participating institutions. JEE Main also serves as the qualifying examination for JEE Advanced, which is the gateway to admission in IITs (Indian Institutes of Technology). The examination is conducted twice a year (January and April sessions) in Computer Based Test (CBT) mode.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: All applicants — must have passed or be appearing in Class 12 or equivalent with required subjects
verifiedConditions.claim: The candidate must have passed Class 12 or equivalent examination with Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects, along with one of Chemistry, Biotechnology, Biology, or any other technical vocational subject, or be appearing in the same in the current year.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: All applicants — must have passed Class 12 in the last three years or be appearing in the current year
verifiedConditions.claim: Candidates who have passed Class 12 or equivalent examination in 2024 or 2025, or are appearing in 2026, are eligible. Candidates who passed before 2024 are not eligible.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: All applicants — maximum 6 attempts across 3 consecutive years (2 sessions per year)
verifiedConditions.claim: A candidate can attempt JEE Main for a maximum of three consecutive years, with two sessions each year, giving a maximum of six attempts. Both sessions in a year count towards the attempt limit.

unverifiedEligibility: There is no upper age limit for appearing in JEE Main as per the latest NTA notification.
For admission to NITs, IIITs, and CFTIs, candidates must secure at least 75% marks in Class 12 (65% for SC/ST) or be in the top 20 percentile of their board.
Diploma holders may be eligible for Paper 2 (B.Arch/B.Planning) under specific conditions.

requirements.claim: Valid Aadhaar card number for Indian citizens. Candidates from Jammu & Kashmir, Meghalaya, and Assam may use alternative valid identity documents such as passport, ration card, or bank account details.

Recent passport-sized photograph (white background, 10 KB to 200 KB, JPG/JPEG format) and scanned signature (4 KB to 30 KB, JPG/JPEG format) as per NTA specifications. Photograph must show the candidate's face clearly with name and date visible on the print.
Class 10 passing certificate or equivalent as proof of date of birth. The date of birth as recorded in the Class 10 certificate is taken as final and no subsequent changes are permitted.

Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS) issued by the competent authority in the prescribed format. PwD certificate from a Government medical board. These certificates are required at the time of counselling and admission for candidates claiming reservation benefits.

Valid and unique email address and active mobile number. All communications from NTA including OTP verification, application confirmation, admit card release, and result notification are sent to the registered email and mobile number.

Selection of examination paper: Paper 1 (B.E./B.Tech) for engineering, Paper 2A (B.Arch) for architecture, or Paper 2B (B.Planning) for planning. Candidates may apply for one or more papers in the same registration. Paper 1 is conducted in CBT mode; Paper 2A includes a drawing section.

processInformation.appliesTo: All new applicants for the session
processInformation.claim: Register on the JEE Main portal (jeemain.nta.nic.in) by providing name, email, mobile number, and date of birth. A system-generated application number and password are provided upon successful registration. Candidates must register separately for each session (January and April).

Complete the online application form with personal details, academic qualifications, paper selection (Paper 1/2A/2B), preferred examination cities (up to four choices), and category/reservation details. Upload scanned photograph, signature, and Class 10 certificate as per NTA specifications.

Pay the examination fee online through debit card, credit card, net banking, or UPI. For Paper 1 (B.E./B.Tech): General — Rs. 1,000, General-EWS/OBC-NCL — Rs. 900, SC/ST/PwD/Third Gender — Rs. 500. For Paper 2A or 2B: General — Rs. 1,000, SC/ST/PwD — Rs. 500. For both papers combined, the fees are additive. An additional GST of 18% is applicable. Fee is non-refundable.

Download the admit card from the JEE Main portal approximately 15 days before each session's examination date. The admit card contains examination centre details, roll number, date and shift, and instructions. Candidates must carry the admit card along with a valid photo ID to the examination centre. The CBT examination is conducted across multiple shifts over several days.

output.claim: Upon result declaration, candidates receive a JEE Main scorecard containing NTA score (percentile-based), All India Rank (AIR), and category rank. Candidates who appear in both sessions are awarded the better of the two NTA scores. The scorecard is used for admission to NITs, IIITs, and CFTIs through JoSAA (Joint Seat Allocation Authority) counselling. Top 2,50,000 rank holders in Paper 1 become eligible to appear for JEE Advanced for admission to IITs.

fees.applicability: Examination fee for Paper 1 (B.E./B.Tech) for General/Unreserved category candidates (per session)
fees.claim: The examination fee for Paper 1 (B.E./B.Tech) per session is Rs. 1,000 for General category, Rs. 900 for General-EWS/OBC-NCL, and Rs. 500 for SC/ST/PwD/Third Gender candidates, plus 18% GST. Indian candidates from abroad pay Rs. 5,000 plus GST. The fee is payable separately for each session and is non-refundable.

fees.applicability: Examination fee for Paper 1 (B.E./B.Tech) for SC/ST/PwD/Third Gender category candidates (per session)
fees.claim: Reduced examination fee of Rs. 500 plus 18% GST (total approximately Rs. 590) per session for Paper 1 for candidates belonging to SC, ST, PwD, and Third Gender categories. Fee concession is applicable upon declaration of valid category at the time of registration.

processingTime.applicability: Registration window duration for each session from opening to closing of application
processingTime.claim: The JEE Main registration window for each session is typically open for 30 to 45 days. Results are declared within 15-30 days after the examination. The January session registration typically opens in November, and the April session registration opens in February. Admit cards are released approximately 15 days before the examination.

sources.title: JEE Main Official Portal — National Testing Agency
sources.publisher: National Testing Agency, Ministry of Education, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The JEE Main official portal provides registration, application form submission, admit card download, answer key challenge, and result declaration for the Joint Entrance Examination Main. The portal publishes the official information bulletin with detailed eligibility criteria, fee structure, exam pattern, syllabus, and session schedule.
claimsSupported: JEE Main is conducted twice a year in January and April sessions.
Examination is in CBT mode for Paper 1 (B.E./B.Tech).
Fee is Rs. 1,000 for General, Rs. 900 for OBC-NCL/EWS, Rs. 500 for SC/ST/PwD.
Top 2,50,000 rank holders qualify for JEE Advanced.
Maximum three consecutive years and six attempts are permitted.
sources.uncertainty: Fee structure, number of sessions per year, and attempt limits may change with future notifications.

sources.title: National Testing Agency — Official Website
sources.publisher: National Testing Agency, Ministry of Education, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: NTA is the autonomous body under the Ministry of Education responsible for conducting JEE Main along with other national entrance examinations. The NTA website provides general information about examination schedules, policies, grievance redressal, and normalization methodology used for multi-session examinations.
claimsSupported: NTA uses percentile-based normalization for multi-session papers.
Best of two session scores is considered for ranking.
Counselling for NITs/IIITs/CFTIs is conducted by JoSAA.
Category certificates must be in prescribed format from competent authority.
sources.uncertainty: NTA policies on normalization methodology and session scheduling may be revised.

limitations: The examination pattern, fee structure, and number of sessions per year are subject to change with each year's official notification.
This record covers the registration process only and does not detail the JoSAA counselling or JEE Advanced registration process.
Attempt limits and year-of-passing eligibility may change based on NTA notification.
The record does not cover Paper 2A (B.Arch) drawing test specifics or Paper 2B (B.Planning) in detail.
Admission eligibility criteria (75% marks / top 20 percentile in Class 12) for NITs/IIITs/CFTIs are separate from JEE Main eligibility.
State-level institutions accepting JEE Main scores may have their own additional eligibility criteria and counselling processes.
